ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure marks three-phase voltages, respectively 200∠0° V, 200∠-120° V, 200∠120° V; the right side is a delta-connected load composed of three identical impedances Z. An ammeter A is connected in series in the upper line, used to measure that phase line current; there is also a voltmeter V near the bottom branch. Each delta branch is labeled Z. Reasoning: Given Z = 8 + j6 Ω, therefore |Z| = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 Ω. The magnitude of each phase of the three-phase voltage given in the figure is 200 V. For a balanced three-phase system, each branch of the delta load bears the line voltage, whose magnitude |V_LL| = sqrt(3) × 200 V. Therefore the current magnitude of each delta branch |I_delta| = |V_LL| / |Z| = (sqrt(3) × 200) / 10 = 20sqrt(3) A. For a balanced delta load, the line current magnitude is sqrt(3) times the branch current, so |I_line| = sqrt(3) × 20sqrt(3) = 60 A. The ammeter is in the upper line, and its reading is the magnitude of that line current.

method.method_draft: From the image identify a balanced delta-connected load of three equal impedances Z and the ammeter measuring the top line current. From the text use Z = 8 + j6 Ω, so |Z| = 10 Ω. The supply phase voltages shown have magnitude 200 V, so the delta branch voltage magnitude is |V_LL| = √3·200 V. Branch current magnitude is |I_delta| = |V_LL|/|Z| = (√3·200)/10. For a balanced delta, line current magnitude is |I_line| = √3|I_delta| = √3·(√3·200/10) = 60 A, which is the ammeter reading.
